items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: you’re not going to have a sixth grade kid, you know, improvising like John Coltrane

ctx.x: And it sounds like you eased into it and so that you weren’t afraid of it. I know, I taught a lot of junior high kids and the idea of improvising was frightening. And I think it’s partly because they didn’t have that experience you’re talking about, that the music was around them.

Very, very good point. I see that and have seen that in my years teaching. I’ve always felt that younger students have an innate creative ability to, what we would call improvise, in many different ways. You see that in art work, you see that in their speaking. The thing about offering jazz improv “quote quote” to let’s say a fifth or sixth grader, okay, is — it can be as you say very, very intimidating. Students, and you know this, at that age, you know, they don’t want to be ridiculed and they don’t want to be…
